title: Emergence Simulator (Flocking)
description: Watch coordinated flock-level movement appear from agents that each follow only local rules, with no central controller.
creator: Systems Thinking in the Age of AI
author: Dan McCreary
subject: Systems Thinking in the Age of AI
Mental Models and Systems Analysis Tools
chapter_title: Mental Models and Systems Analysis Tools

educational.learningObjective: Given a flock of simple agents each following local rules, the learner will explain how coordinated, flock-level movement emerges with no central controller.
prerequisites: Knows what an agent is in a simulation
Has seen at least one system whose behavior comes from interactions rather than parts
learningOutcomes: Explain emergence as behavior of the whole that is not present in any part
Describe how local rules can produce a global pattern
Recognize that the absence of a controller is not the absence of organization
educational.assessmentOpportunity: Ask learners to explain, in two sentences, how the flock moves as a unit when no agent knows what the flock is doing. A correct answer references local interaction rather than shared information.

pedagogical.feedbackType: Continuous visual feedback as the global pattern forms
misconceptionsAddressed: That coordinated behavior requires a leader
That the whole's behavior can be read off from a single agent's rules
discussionQuestions: Traffic jams form with no one organizing them. What are the local rules?
If emergence needs no controller, what does a manager actually add to an organization?
Can emergent behavior be designed, or only encouraged?
